stemBlocks: A small slider of mass $30 \text{ g}$ is at rest near the bottom of a frictionless slope and in contact with a light uncompressed spring as shown.

The spring is compressed by $5.0 \text{ cm}$ and the slider remains in contact with it.
The spring is released and causes the slider to rise up the slope to a maximum vertical height of $20 \text{ cm}$.
The slider is replaced with one of mass $20 \text{ g}$.
The spring is now compressed by $15 \text{ cm}$, and the new slider remains in contact with it.
To what maximum vertical height does this new slider rise after it is released?
(the spring obeys Hooke's law; assume that air resistance is negligible)
